title: std::array and Fixed-Size Collections
learningObjectives: Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: std::array<T,N> is fixed-size, preserves its size, and supports container operations and checked at() access.
understand.whyItMatters: It gives fixed collections a convenient standard-library interface.
understand.explain: Use size, iteration, and at() where bounds checking is useful.

examples.title: Create array
examples.explanation: size reports the fixed number of elements.

examples.title: Checked access
examples.explanation: at checks bounds and throws on an invalid index.

examples.title: Read elements
examples.explanation: Const reference traversal avoids copying and mutation.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five std::array and Fixed-Size Collections examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating std::array and fixed-size collections. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.
